plates.text_on_crop: Dee's note above the letters (tentative reading; words in [] uncertain): 'he drewe the blak uppon, and so the yelow cullor d[i]sapearing / there remayned only the shape of the letter in blak. after this manner. / and iuſt [= just] of this quantitie and proportion.' The sentence begins before the crop. ('iuſt' is one word on the page - the u written like an n; it was earlier split as 'in [just?]'.)

plates.table: 'The HOLY TABLE' (engraving): 84 angelic letters in the boxed border (21 per side between corner marks) and 12 in the central 3 x 4 grid - Wellcome copy 1
plates.layout: Border boxes, one letter per box (21 per side between corner boxes); the four corner boxes hold a diagonal V-with-curl mark (see corner_marks); central grid of 12 large letters, 4 rows x 3 columns. Border letters face the centre of the table (see orientation). No values or names are printed beside any angelic letter on the plate (the seven small square and round figures on the table carry roman letters and numerals of their own, not a key to the angelic letters).

plates.shorthand_key: visual shorthand only, describing each letter turned so that its top is up; on the plate every border letter stands with its top toward the centre of the table (top border upside down as the page is held, right border tops pointing left, left border tops pointing right, bottom border and centre upright). plates.shorthand_key: visual shorthand only, describing each letter turned so that its top is up; on the plate every border letter stands with its top toward the centre of the table (top border upside down as the page is held, right border tops pointing left, left border tops pointing right, bottom border and centre upright). Tokens: 7 = top bar and straight stem ending in a flared foot; 7h = top bar and a stem that curves down to a pointed hook on the right; Z = top bar, stem and a foot turned to the right; ⅃ = slanted L (oblique stroke on a curved base sweeping right); Є = C-curve opening right, with a two-pronged bar across its back (left side); Э = the same reversed (opening left, bar across its back on the right, barb pointing inward); 6 = hooked bowl; X = X with curved arms; ẋ = upright zigzag crossed form like Ж with hooked ends; ẋd = oblique stroke hooked at the top right, crossed by two short bars near its foot (distinct from ẋ); Ω = arch on out-turned feet; P = P with a crossbar through the stem; ε = plain epsilon; εb = epsilon with a long beak projecting right from its waist and a curled top (whether ε and εb are different letters the plate does not say); V = V with the right arm curled; ( = single curved stroke, heavy at the lower left; a = hooked arch on two feet. The tokens L, 9, 3 and U used before the check were upside-down readings of 7, 6, ε/εb and a. Not a reading: the plate prints no values

plates.orientation: Every border letter stands with its top toward the centre of the table, so each side reads upright to someone standing at that side. plates.copy_note: In this copy the plate's left edge runs into the binding fold: the left frame line and the first two cells of the grid row ('1', '2') are not in the crop. The heading itself - title, the three angelic words and the roman readings - is complete and agrees glyph for glyph with copy 1.

legibility: Sloane MS 3188, f. 104: every one of the 21 forms (and the small form above the 10th of the upper line) is complete and sharp, but the image is a high-contrast black-and-white rendering of unknown provenance (it looks thresholded from a photograph or microfilm), and only Wikimedia's 1920 px rendering could be fetched (the 4303 px original was refused with HTTP 429, repeatedly). Sloane MS 3189: all 21 forms present and readable but small and soft (1085 px original). Casaubon 1659: both Wellcome copies are sharp colour scans at about 3600-4200 px a page; every border box, the 12 central letters and the angelic words of the Specimen heading are complete in copy 1; copy 2 loses part of the Holy Table's left border in the binding fold.
problems: No image of either manuscript from the British Library itself could be obtained: the BL catalogue lists Sloane MSS 3188, 3189 and 3191 as digitised but '(digital images currently unavailable)', and access.bl.uk and api.bl.uk (the BL viewer and IIIF) refused the connection (HTTP 502 at the proxy). Sloane MS 3677 (Ashmole's copy) is not digitised.

The only manuscript images reachable are two Wikimedia Commons crops whose photographer and source are not stated. Their folio attributions (f. 104; 'r. 57') come from the Commons descriptions and cannot be checked on the crops, which show no folio numbers.

Neither manuscript crop shows any label: the forms stand alone, with no letter names and no Latin values beside them. The table of names and values the research file describes is not on these crops. Every 'value' is therefore null; the 'research_order_name_unverified' field applies the research file's unconfirmed order and is NOT a reading of the page.

Casaubon (1659) prints no alphabet table. The letters appear only (a) on the Holy Table engraving (96 letters, unlabelled) and (b) in the heading of the Specimen plate (three angelic words beside the roman readings 'Pagesgem' and 'Bacap Laſſos'). Word 1 has 8 glyphs for the 8 letters of 'Pagesgem', and word 3 has 5 glyphs for 'Bacap', but word 2 has 5 glyphs against the 6 letters of 'Laſſos', so the print does not support a glyph-by-glyph pairing; use it only as corroboration.

Wikimedia's servers answered HTTP 429 to the original files of both Commons images and to the Commons API after the first few calls; the files here are Wikimedia's own 1920 px and 1280 px renderings (the 1280 px Sloane 3189 file is upscaled from a 1085 px original).
notes: Sloane MS 3188 f. 104 crop, read right to left as the script runs: the upper line holds 11 forms and the lower line 10. The smaller form written above the second form from the right of the upper line (a B-like form above a B-like form) is on the page and should be recorded as a second form or correction; the page does not say which.

Sloane MS 3189 crop: the same 21 forms are written LEFT TO RIGHT in 14 + 7 with dots between them, in the same sequence the f. 104 forms give when read right to left; there is no extra form above the B-like letter.

Dee's note on the f. 104 crop speaks of the 'yelow cullor' (yellow colour) over which the letter was drawn in black; this bears on the research file's 'light yellow colour' lead (the words 'light yellow' are not on this crop; the sentence begins earlier).

Casaubon's Preface (read in the TCP transcription A37412 and confirmed in the OCR of the Getty copy, truefaithfulrela00deej) says of the Holy Table: 'This Table ... is preserved and to be seen in Sir Thomas Cottons Library ... and by his leave is here represented in a brass Cut'; of the Specimen: 'There were many Tables or Schemes at the end of the Book, containing Letters, a. b. c. &c. disposed into little squares, with an Inscription over each Table in that unknown Character (before spoken of) expressed in usual Letters how it should be read. There is one for a Specimen here at the end of the Preface'.

Casaubon's Preface also claims the characters 'are no other, for the most part but such as were set out and published long agoe by one Theseus Ambrosus out of Magical books ... Some letters are the same, others have much resemblace' - a 1659 comparison with 'Theseus Ambrosius' (Teseo Ambrogio; the book meant is presumably his Introductio in Chaldaicam linguam, Pavia 1539 - general knowledge, not checked), reported as Casaubon's claim. The passage was read in the TCP transcription and confirmed in the OCR of the Getty copy (truefaithfulrela00deej_djvu.txt).

The grid of Casaubon's Specimen table is printed in roman letters and numerals (with an inner circle of capitals and numbers), not in the angelic character; only its heading uses the angelic character.
Other plates in the same preliminaries (the circular 'Septentrio / Oriens / Meridies / Occidens' plate at copy 1 n78) carry no angelic letters.
The Getty Research Institute copy on archive.org (truefaithfulrela00deej) was not used; its IIIF server timed out and the two Wellcome copies already give two impressions of both plates.
